title: autotune: default batching/caching heuristics + quantization profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Summary: Adds an autotune pipeline that suggests and applies safe defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching, introduces model-driven quantization profiles, and ships a unit-economics CLI and console dashboard to help teams evaluate cost/latency tradeoffs. Motivation: Many customers see significant cost variance across workloads because defaults are conservative. This change automates workload profiling, recommends batching/cache defaults tuned per route, and exposes a developer-friendly unit-econ surface so teams can evaluate the dollar/token impact of config changes. High level: 1) Runtime: new heuristic-based scheduler and batching policy module that consumes per-route telemetry and applies per-request batching TTLs, max_batch_size suggestions, and prefix cache retention heuristics; includes safe rollouts and runtime feature flags. 2) Quantization: model registry extension that stores quantization profiles (fp16/int8/4bit candidates) with estimated quality impact and CPU/GPU performance delta, plus a CLI to run quick offline evals against canonical prompts. 3) Unit-econ tooling: a redwood uecon CLI to compute cost/latency delta from config changes and a console dashboard for comparing profiles and projected monthly spend. Checklist: [x] workload profiler + telemetry export; [x] batching/caching heuristics and rollout config; [x] quant profiles schema + registry integration; [x] uecon CLI and console endpoints; [x] tests: unit + integration + perf smoke; [x] docs and migration notes. Links: Linear ENG-1264 for autotune design, ENG-1302 for quant profiles, PRs with related perf benchmarks in /benchmark-lab. Migration notes: a lightweight DB migration adds a quant_profiles table and a per-route autotune_state column. Backwards compatibility: defaults are only applied when route opt-in is enabled; rollout uses existing canary/percent-based rollouts to avoid sudden behavior changes.
commit_summary: 1) feat(autotune): add workload profiler and export pipeline; 2) feat(runtime): batching heuristic engine + safe rollout hooks; 3) feat(registry): quant_profile schema + import tool; 4) feat(uecon): CLI + dashboard endpoints; 5) chore(test): add perf smoke and integration tests; 6) docs: api/console usage and migration guide
review_comments: Ethan Moore: Overall looks good, appreciate the safe rollout plans. One ask: can batching decisions be bounded by per-tenant SLOs so we don't increase p99 unexpectedly?
Priya Kapoor (author): Added tenant-level SLO caps to batching_policy.go and unit tests to cover p95/p99 guards; added tests to perf smoke to validate p99 under synthetic load.
Sofia Li: The quant profile schema looks fine; please add an explicit quality-metric field and a recommended fallback when degradation > 2%
Priya Kapoor (author): Added quality_metric and fallback_profile fields to the schema; migration script updated and docs note on fallback behavior included.
Marcos Alvarez: CI integration flaked on the first run (integration test timeout). I reran after small timing tweak in the test harness and all checks passed.
Ethan Moore: Approved after verifying that the dashboard surfaces the expected cost deltas and that rollout controls are present.

release_notes: Automated autotune defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching; model quantization profiles in registry with fallback rules; new 'redwood uecon' CLI and console dashboard for unit-economics analysis; DB migration to add quant_profiles table; opt-in rollouts with tenant SLO guards; see docs/autotune.md and docs/uecon_cli.md for usage and migration steps.
